decisions.reason: As a close-to-core carpet with no negative market signal yet, it is still a live option worth keeping, although the firm's broad portfolio and several similar launches create some pruning risk.

This premium hand-knotted carpet fits the firm's craftsmanship positioning, but as a more niche and potentially costlier offer in a broad range it faces a somewhat higher chance of being rationalized if demand proves limited.

Because it is another close-to-core decorative carpet and there is no evidence that its value has clearly failed to materialize, management would usually keep it for now, though overlap with other carpet options raises the likelihood of later withdrawal.

A corner bench extends the established furniture range in a way that suits the firm's interior expertise, and furniture lines in this segment are typically worth keeping while market acceptance is still being learned.

This low-pile carpet is inexpensive to keep as an option relative to a full new platform, but the firm's already broad assortment and multiple nearby carpet introductions make it somewhat exposed to portfolio cleanup.

The swivel shell chair line is close to the firm's core and relevant to flexible workplace concepts, so despite some model-complexity costs it is likely to be retained while uncertainty about its full potential remains.
